==Problem==
In this addition problem, each letter stands for a different digit.

<math> \setlength{\tabcolsep}{0.5mm}\begin{array}{cccc}&T & W & O\\ +&T & W & O\\ \hline F& O & U & R\end{array} </math>

If T = 7 and the letter O represents an even number, what is the only possible value for W?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 0\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 1\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 2\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 3\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 4 </math>

==Solution==
Since both <imath>T</imath>'s are <imath>7</imath>, then <imath>O</imath> has to equal <imath>4</imath>, because <imath>7 + 7 = 14</imath>. Then, <imath>F</imath> has to equal <imath>1</imath>. To get <imath>R</imath>, we do <imath>4 + 4</imath> (since <imath>O = 4</imath>) to get <imath>R = 8</imath>. The value for <imath>W</imath> then has to be a number less than <imath>5</imath>, otherwise it will change the value of <imath>O</imath>, and can't be a number that has already been used, like <imath>4</imath> or <imath>1</imath>. The only other possibilities are <imath>2</imath> and <imath>3</imath>. <imath>2</imath> doesn't work because it makes <imath>U = 4</imath>, which is what <imath>O</imath> already equals. So, the only possible value of <imath>W</imath> is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 3}</imath>
